title: Dust and bones, raised again? They could not believe it.
subtitle: The doubt that dust can live

row.title: Who is doing it
sub: the One who made the heavens

then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}thought it unlikely and did not believe it.{/trap} Just before this, Allah reminded them that the heavens are harder to create than they are. Their doubt looked at the dust, not at the Creator.
now: You stand at a burial and watch the soil go in. It feels so final. {idea}The question is not how little is left, but how great is the One who raises.{/idea}
old: Once a body is dust, there is nothing left to bring back.
new: The resurrection depends on Allah's power, not on what remains of me.
try: Make dua today for someone you have lost, trusting you will meet again.

title: And our forefathers too? Yes, them too.
subtitle: The oldest generations are not forgotten
then: The deniers added a second question: {trap}and also our fathers of old?{/trap} Ibn Kathir treats it with the previous verse: they thought it unlikely. {idea}The answer in the next verse covers them all.{/idea}
now: You look at an old family photo: great-grandparents whose names nobody remembers. {idea}They will stand up on that Day too{/idea}, and so will you, and your grandchildren.
old: The people of long ago are simply gone.
new: Every generation, however old, will be raised and meet its Lord.
try: Make dua today for your grandparents and those before them by name, if you know them.

title: Say: Yes, and you will be humbled.
subtitle: A short answer to a long doubt
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to answer: {idea}yes, you will be raised{/idea} after becoming dust and bones, and {trap}put to shame before His great might.{/trap} He links it to 27:87: all shall come to Him humbled.
now: Someone at work talks big, never admits a mistake, laughs at religion. You might be that person sometimes. {idea}Everyone comes to Him humble in the end.{/idea} Choosing humility now is easier.
old: Admitting I am small makes me weak.
new: Humbling myself before Allah now is better than being humbled later.
try: Admit one small mistake to someone today, plainly, without excuses.

title: One shout, and they are standing, staring.
subtitle: No time between the call and the gathering
then: Ibn Kathir says it will be {idea}a single command from Allah{/idea}: He calls them once to come out of the earth, and they stand before Him, {trap}staring at the horrors of the Day.{/trap}
now: A phone call at 3am. One sentence, and your whole life changes. You know that feeling. {idea}The Day will come like that: one call, no build-up.{/idea} So the getting ready happens now.
old: I will have time to prepare when the end gets closer.
new: It comes with a single call, so today is my time to prepare.
try: Do one thing today you would want done if you knew the call was close.

title: Woe to us, this is the Day of Recompense.
subtitle: Regret that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says they will {trap}blame themselves and admit they wronged themselves{/trap}, filled with regret when regret no longer helps. They see with their own eyes what they had mocked.
now: You snapped at your mother and she went quiet. That night you feel the sting. {reward}That sting, today, is a gift.{/reward} Regret while there is time can still become an apology, a change, a tawbah.
old: Regret is just a bad feeling to push away.
new: Regret now is a mercy, because now it can still turn into repentance.
try: Turn one regret into action today: an apology, a repayment, or a sincere istighfar.

title: This is the Day of Sorting you used to deny.
subtitle: The day everything is separated out

row.title: you denied it
sub: used to call it a lie

then: Ibn Kathir says the angels and believers will say this {trap}as a rebuke{/trap}. Then Allah will command the angels to {idea}separate the disbelievers from the believers{/idea} where they stand.
now: In life things blur: who was right in the argument, whose money it really was, whether that comment was a joke. {idea}That Day, everything gets sorted cleanly.{/idea} Live as if the sorting is honest, because it will be.
old: Things are so blurry that no one will ever know who was really right.
new: Allah will sort everything clearly, so I can be honest now.
try: Settle one blurry matter today: return something, or tell the truth about something.

title: Gather the wrongdoers with their kind.
subtitle: You end up with the people like you
then: Umar and others said azwaj means {idea}those who are like them{/idea}: people of the same sin gathered together. Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}their friends.{/idea} Their idols are gathered with them too.
now: Look at the five people you spend the most time with, online and off. What do you talk about? What do you laugh at? {idea}You are slowly becoming their kind, and they yours.{/idea}
old: Who I hang out with does not say anything about me.
new: I will be gathered with my kind, so I choose my company carefully.
try: Spend some time today with one person who makes you a better Muslim.

title: Guide them now, to the path of Fire.
subtitle: The bitter end of refusing guidance
then: Ibn Kathir explains it as {trap}take them to the way to Hell.{/trap} The word used is guide, the same word as the guidance they turned away from all their lives.
now: Every day you choose what leads you: the next video, a friend's opinion, your mood, or the Quran. {idea}Something is always guiding you.{/idea} The verse asks you to choose that guide now.
old: I am not following anyone; I just do my own thing.
new: I am always being led by something, so I want Allah to be my guide.
try: Say ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim slowly and with meaning in your next prayer.

title: Stop them. They will be questioned.
subtitle: Every life comes with questions

row.title: questioned
sub: about what they did and said

then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}detain them, for they are to be brought to account.{/idea} Uthman bin Zaidah said the first thing a man will be asked about is {trap}the company he kept.{/trap}
now: A job interview: they stop you and ask, why did you leave your last job? You need an answer ready. {idea}There will be questions about how you spent your life{/idea}, and you can prepare your answers now.
old: Life just passes, and nobody asks about it.
new: I will be stopped and asked, so I want my answers to be good ones.
try: Before bed, ask yourself one question: how did I spend today? Answer honestly.

title: Why don't you help each other now?
subtitle: Promises of loyalty that vanish
then: Ibn Kathir says this is said {trap}by way of rebuke{/trap}: you claimed you would all help one another. The Quraysh were proud of their tribal loyalty. {trap}On that Day, no tribe will help.{/trap}
now: Your friends say they have your back, the group that always covers for each other's lies at work or at school. {trap}That loyalty has an end date.{/trap} On that Day no one can carry anyone.
old: My friends will always cover for me.
new: Only my deeds and Allah's mercy help me there, so I should not lean on cover-ups.
try: If you are covering for something wrong for a friend, think about how to stop gently.

title: That Day, they simply surrender.
subtitle: When resistance runs out

row.title: surrendered
sub: no way to resist or avoid

then: Ibn Kathir says they will be {trap}subjected to the command of Allah{/trap} and unable to resist or avoid it. People who refused to submit in life will have no choice but to submit then.
now: You argue with every rule: at work, at home, in faith. You hold out. {trap}Eventually everyone gives in to Allah's command.{/trap} {reward}Choosing to give in now is what Islam means.{/reward}
new: Everyone submits in the end; submitting willingly now is the honour.
try: Pick one command of Allah you resist and follow it today, willingly.

title: They turn to each other, and the blaming starts.
subtitle: Followers and leaders, face to face
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers will {trap}blame one another{/trap} at the Resurrection, as they will argue in Hell. He cites 40:47 and 34:31, where the weak blame the arrogant and the arrogant push it back.
now: Something goes wrong at work and the meeting turns into finger pointing: you said, no you said. {idea}Blame passed around does not make it lighter.{/idea} Each person still owns their part.
old: If someone else talked me into it, it is on them.
new: I own my choices, even the ones others pushed me toward.
try: The next time something goes wrong today, name your own part first.

title: You came at us from the right side.
subtitle: How wrong is made to look right
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {trap}you forced us with your power{/trap}. As-Suddi said you made {trap}falsehood look attractive{/trap} and stopped us seeing the truth. Qatadah said you blocked every good deed.
now: Nobody says, come do something wrong. They say: it is just business, everyone does it, you deserve a treat. {trap}Wrong arrives dressed as right.{/trap} The verse warns you about the right-hand approach.
old: I will know something is wrong because it will look wrong.
new: Wrong often comes looking reasonable, so I look at where it leads.
try: Notice one thing today that is sold to you as harmless. Ask where it actually leads.

title: No, you were never believers yourselves.
subtitle: The leaders throw the blame back
then: Ibn Kathir says the leaders will tell their followers, {trap}it is not as you say; your hearts denied faith{/trap} and were open to disbelief and sin. Those once trusted now turn against them.
now: The friend who got you into a habit is the first to say, I never forced you. And they are partly right. {idea}Someone can open the door, but you walk through it.{/idea}
old: I only went along because of them.
new: Others can invite me, but my heart decides whether to accept.
try: Think of one bad habit you blame on someone else. Own it, and ask Allah for help to leave it.

title: We had no power over you. You were transgressors.
subtitle: No one can force a heart

row.title: you transgressed
sub: you chose us over the prophets

then: Ibn Kathir says the leaders admit: {trap}we had no proof of what we called you to.{/trap} You responded to us and {idea}neglected the truth the prophets brought with proof.{/idea}
now: The influencer you trusted had no evidence, just confidence. The prophets brought clear signs. {idea}You chose who to listen to.{/idea} You can still choose differently.
old: They seemed so sure of themselves, so I followed.
new: Confidence is not proof; I follow those who bring the truth.
try: Unfollow or mute one voice today that pulls you away from Allah.
